synthesis.summary: Upper Hunter Shire Council is a regional NSW council (Smart City, with Energy & Utilities as a secondary fit). It is an End User running five water supply schemes, sewerage systems and an IT network of 40-plus sites. Its WAN and firewall work is supported by Atturra. The evidence shows a Teltonika-relevant footprint: distributed water and sewer assets, a 2022 SCADA/telemetry upgrade in Merriwa and Cassilis, and 4G failover at some sites. However, no current, confirmed connectivity or telemetry project was found. The strongest live development is the council's water-quality program, supported by quote_verified cards. It covers UV disinfection 'coming soon', a joint Scone/Muswellbrook water treatment facility (about $80M) under work since 2023, and a sewage treatment plant replacement (about $50M). It follows two extended boil water alerts in 2025. The large plants are unfunded and depend on grants, and no comms component is confirmed. The adopted 2026–29 Delivery Program and the September 2026 committee papers could not be read, so it is unknown whether telemetry or comms items are budgeted. Overall this is a medium-strength account: credible reasons to talk exist, but there is no strong recent Sales Trigger.

triggers.title: Water treatment upgrade program: UV disinfection, joint water treatment facility and sewage treatment plant replacement
triggers.scale: Supplies Scone, Aberdeen and Murrurundi. Estimated $78–80M capital cost for UHSC alone, about $80M for the joint water plant plus about $50M for sewage treatment plant replacement. Projects are unfunded and depend on grants.
triggers.fact: Council supplies Scone, Aberdeen and Murrurundi directly from Glenbawn Dam with chlorination only. It says UV disinfection is coming soon and there is no filtration plant. Since 2023 it has worked with Muswellbrook Shire Council on a joint water treatment facility (E12). The facility would cost about $80M for the water plant and a further $50M to replace the ageing sewage treatment plant. Council says these projects are not affordable without significant external grant funding (E11). The supply had two extended boil water alerts in 2025, and the estimated capital cost for Upper Hunter Shire alone is $78–80M (E13). The October 2023 committee agenda lists the joint Scone Water Treatment Plant under Water & Sewer capital works, with a BECA preliminary feasibility review of the Brushy Hill site (E14). The April 2023 agenda says the Scone Sewerage Treatment Plant is proposed to be replaced or upgraded, depending on funding (E15).
triggers.inference: New treatment equipment such as UV disinfection, and any future treatment plant, would typically need monitoring and control. That may have to integrate with the council's existing water and sewer telemetry. None of the cards mention connectivity, telemetry or comms for these projects. The large plants are unfunded, so timing is uncertain. The UV disinfection item is the most near-term element, but its current status is unconfirmed. The core cards are quote_verified, but they date from 2025, so the information is over 12 months old.
triggers.possibleOpportunity: Worth exploring how monitoring and communications are being planned for the UV disinfection work and any future treatment assets, and whether these will tie into existing telemetry.
triggers.whyNow: Water quality is clearly a live, high-profile issue for the council after the 2025 boil water alerts. The UV disinfection was described as 'coming soon', and the adopted 2026–27 Operational Plan (E7) may carry related capital works. The evidence is over 12 months old, so current status should be confirmed in conversation.

triggers.scale: 40-plus sites across the WAN, with two supplier WANs and 4G failover at some sites
triggers.fact: Atturra's client story says the council's in-house Information Services team uses Atturra for networking and infrastructure projects. Atturra helped manage and troubleshoot 40-plus sites, internet access across the WAN, firewalling, and a refresh of core and edge switches (E5). After security breaches, the council split its IT systems across two supplier WANs, with some sites also using 4G for failover where appropriate (E6).

triggers.scale: All water and sewer sites in Merriwa and Cassilis; budget $71,000 against $83,129
triggers.fact: The June 2022 Infrastructure Services Committee agenda lists a water and sewer SCADA/Telemetry upgrade at all sites in Merriwa and Cassilis. It is shown as 98% complete with final set-up work remaining, with a listed budget of $71,000 against $83,129 (E4).
triggers.inference: This confirms the council runs SCADA/telemetry across distributed water and sewer sites. It is historical background rather than a current trigger. The comms method (radio or cellular) is unknown. Evidence is tool_source only.
triggers.possibleOpportunity: Could be worth asking how the telemetry network communicates today and whether the other schemes (Scone, Aberdeen, Murrurundi) have been or will be upgraded similarly.
triggers.whyNow: No current timing. This is useful context that supports a telemetry-focused question alongside T1.

triggers.title: Adopted Delivery Program 2026–2029 and Operational Plan 2026–27, and the September 2026 Infrastructure Services report
triggers.scale: Annual budget and capital works program, contents unknown
triggers.fact: At its 29 June 2026 meeting, council adopted the Delivery Program 2026 to 2029 and Operational Plan 2026 to 2027, including the annual budget and capital works program (E7). The draft was on public exhibition from 30 April to 29 May 2026 (E8). The 28 September 2026 Ordinary Meeting agenda reports on the 8 September 2026 Infrastructure Services Committee meeting and names Stephen Hitchens as Director Infrastructure Services and responsible officer (E10).
triggers.inference: These are recent and genuine, and the new capital works program could contain telemetry or water infrastructure items. Its contents could not be read, so no Teltonika relevance is confirmed. Evidence is tool_source only.
triggers.possibleOpportunity: A natural opener to ask which water and sewer infrastructure priorities are in the new capital works program.
triggers.whyNow: Adopted about three months ago, with the first-year capital program now starting delivery.

people.whyRelevant: Director Infrastructure Services and named responsible officer in the September 2026 agenda (E10). His committee covers the water and sewer works program behind T1, T3 and T4, which makes him the best confirmed current contact.

Authored the October 2023 Water & Sewer works program report covering the water treatment plant feasibility (E14). He would be highly relevant to telemetry questions, but it is unconfirmed whether he is still Manager Water & Sewer.

angles.title: Monitoring and communications for the water treatment upgrades
angles.conversationQuestion: As the UV disinfection and treatment upgrades for Scone progress, how are you planning to monitor the new equipment and connect it back to your existing telemetry?
angles.whyItWorks: It refers to the council's most visible, quote_verified water-quality priority and asks about a likely telemetry need without assuming one exists.

angles.title: 4G failover across the council's site network
angles.conversationQuestion: How is 4G failover working across your sites today, and are there remote sites where connectivity is still a headache?
angles.whyItWorks: Existing cellular failover across 40-plus sites is a direct connectivity signal, though the source is undated and Atturra may be involved.

angles.title: Telemetry comms across the water and sewer schemes
angles.conversationQuestion: What do your water and sewer telemetry sites use for communications today, radio or cellular?
angles.whyItWorks: It builds on the known Merriwa/Cassilis SCADA upgrade to learn the current comms setup across all five schemes.

angles.title: New capital works program
angles.conversationQuestion: Which water and sewer infrastructure projects are top priority in the newly adopted 2026–27 capital works program?
angles.whyItWorks: It is a recent, genuine opener that helps find out whether connectivity-related works are budgeted.

gaps: Contents of the adopted 2026–27 Operational Plan and capital works program: whether SCADA, telemetry, comms, the water treatment plant, the Aberdeen back-feed or the sewage treatment plant are budgeted (L1, L6). The PDFs could not be read.
What communications (radio or cellular) the water and sewer telemetry sites use, and the current status of the Merriwa/Cassilis upgrade (L2).
Current Manager Water & Sewer. Grahame Wilson (2023) and Greg Longman (2022) are the last names found (L3, L7).
Whether the Atturra relationship is current and what hardware the 4G failover sites use (L4).
Whether UV disinfection at Scone is under way and whether it includes new control or telemetry equipment (L8).
Any recent tenders covering communications, CCTV or SCADA (L5).
No IT or Information Services lead identified for the WAN/4G angle.
No vendor or partner pages, competitor technology or industry sources found (coverage not_found).
Funding status of the joint water treatment facility and sewage treatment plant replacement (grant-dependent).

email.subject: Monitoring for the Scone UV disinfection upgrade
email.body:
Hi Stephen,

I saw Council has UV disinfection coming for the Scone, Aberdeen and Murrurundi supply, on top of the existing chlorination.

Not sure how you're planning to monitor the new equipment and connect it back to your existing telemetry, so I'm interested to understand whether that's something already sorted or still open.

I also saw the SCADA/telemetry upgrade at the Merriwa and Cassilis sites in the 2022 committee agenda, so I'm curious whether Scone would follow a similar approach.

I'm with Teltonika Networks and thought there could be some overlap on the cellular connectivity side.

Would you be available for a quick chat in the next couple of weeks?

Cheers,
